as_told.title: Falasha (Beta Israel) tradition of the Ark's journey to Ethiopia
as_told.place_text: Israel; island in the Nile; Lake Tana, Ethiopia

plain: The Beta Israel, the Jews of Ethiopia, also called the Falashas, have a tradition that their ancestors fled Israel carrying the Ark of the Covenant, the sacred chest of the Bible. As the story goes, they kept it for several hundred years on an island in the Nile, Elephantine in Egypt, then brought it to Ethiopia, by Lake Tana. The writer Graham Hancock tells this on two visits to the show, passing on what the Beta Israel say, and the second time he also points to an Ethiopian text called the Kebra Nagast, all in support of his view that the Ark ended up in Ethiopia.
